title: Beef, loin, top loin steak, boneless, lip‑on, separable lean only, trimmed to 1/8" fat, choice, raw

content.title: About
content.content: A lean cut from the top portion of the beef loin, boneless, with the lip retained. Trimmed to leave only 1/8 inch of fat, classified as "choice" grade and sold raw.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The top loin is considered one of the most tender and prized beef cuts.
It is often used in restaurants for filet‑mignon style preparations.
The retained lip helps keep the steak juicy during cooking.
"Choice" grade indicates high marbling and flavor, though below "prime".
Traditionally the loin is sliced across the grain to maximize tenderness.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Heme iron
items.content: The iron in beef is highly bioavailable, helping prevent iron‑deficiency anemia.

items.title: Vitamin B12
items.content: Essential for nervous system health and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low carbohydrate
items.content: Fits well into low‑carb and keto dietary patterns.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Raw beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella; proper cooking is required.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Even trimmed, the cut contains saturated fats that should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Hyperuricemia
items.content: Large portions of red meat can raise uric acid levels, which may aggravate gout.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The steak can be pan‑seared, grilled, or oven‑roasted. Aim for an internal temperature of 63 °C for medium doneness. Let the meat come to room temperature before cooking, season with salt, and optionally add fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–2 °C in its original packaging for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
